title: Modular semiconductor wafer transport and processing system

features.item: A housing containing a displaceable magnet and pole shoes with workpiece contact surfaces.
features.note: This reference describes a wafer transport system with robotic arms and gate valves, but does not mention a magnetic gripper with a displaceable magnet or pole shoes.

features.item: A magnet displaceable along a direction between a gripping position and a release position.
features.note: The reference describes wafer handling arms and mechanisms for moving wafers, but not a displaceable magnet for gripping.

features.item: Pole shoes attached to the housing, each with a workpiece contact surface.
features.note: There is no mention of pole shoes or workpiece contact surfaces in the context of a magnetic gripper.

features.item: Pole shoes designed to guide a magnetic field portion to the workpiece contact surface.
features.note: The reference does not discuss magnetic fields, pole shoes, or guiding magnetic fields.

features.item: A workpiece contact surface defining a contact surface angle of 170° to 190° with the displacement direction.
features.note: This feature relates to a magnetic gripper, which is not described in the reference.

features.item: A magnetic gripper with housing, displaceable magnet, and pole shoes where contact surface angle is 170° to 190° relative to displacement direction.
features.note: The reference does not describe a magnetic gripper or its specific components and angles.

features.item: A magnetic gripper system with a magnetic gripper and ferromagnetic workpiece, where magnet in gripping position presses workpiece against contact surfaces by magnetic force.
features.note: The reference describes a wafer transport system using robotic arms and clips, not magnetic grippers and ferromagnetic workpieces.

features.item: Housing extending along a longitudinal axis with displacement direction parallel to that axis.
features.note: This feature describes a specific configuration of a magnetic gripper housing, which is not present in the reference.

features.item: Pole shoes with an active structure for directing the magnetic field portion.
features.note: The reference does not mention pole shoes or active structures for directing magnetic fields.

features.item: An active structure with a bevel defining a bevel angle of 5° to 85° with the workpiece contact surface.
features.note: This feature relates to a magnetic gripper, which is not described in the reference.

features.item: An active structure with multiple projections for directing magnetic field and forming the workpiece contact surface.
features.note: The reference does not describe magnetic fields, projections, or workpiece contact surfaces in this context.

features.item: Adjacent first and second projections with a recess between them, recess depth or length deviating by at most 25% from projection length.
features.note: This feature describes specific details of pole shoe projections, which are not present in the reference.

features.item: A positioning device on the magnetic gripper for positioning the ferromagnetic workpiece on the contact surface.
features.note: The reference describes wafer aligners and flat finders for positioning wafers, but not a positioning device on a magnetic gripper.

features.item: First and second pole shoes where the magnet in gripping position makes the first pole shoe act as north pole and second as south pole.
features.note: The reference does not discuss magnetic poles or their configuration.

features.item: A magnet displaceable electrically, pneumatically, or mechanically between gripping and release positions.
features.note: The reference describes mechanisms for moving wafer handling arms, but not a displaceable magnet actuated by electrical, pneumatic, or mechanical means for gripping.

features.item: A position sensor detecting gripping position and/or release position, or a workpiece sensor detecting the ferromagnetic workpiece.
features.note: The reference mentions a master controller circuit and pressure activated switches, but not position sensors for a magnetic gripper or sensors specifically detecting ferromagnetic workpieces.

features.item: Housing with a receptacle for receiving a workpiece sensor and/or a supply line.
features.note: The reference describes various housings and chambers but does not detail receptacles for workpiece sensors or supply lines in the context of a magnetic gripper.

features.item: A manipulator interface on the magnetic gripper for attaching to a manipulator.
features.note: The reference describes wafer handling arms and mechanisms, but not a magnetic gripper with a manipulator interface.

features.item: Housing portion designed to suppress magnetic field escape, or a shielding device to at least partially prevent magnetic field escape.
features.note: The reference does not discuss magnetic fields or shielding devices.

features.item: At least one projection with length deviating by at most 25% from the thickness of the ferromagnetic workpiece.
features.note: This feature describes specific details of pole shoe projections, which are not present in the reference.

features.item: A receptacle in the form of a groove in the housing.
features.note: The reference describes various housing components but does not mention a receptacle in the form of a groove for the purpose described in the feature.

features.item: A bevel angle of 15° to 75° between the active structure bevel and the workpiece contact surface.
features.note: This feature relates to a magnetic gripper, which is not described in the reference.

features.item: A bevel angle of 40° to 60° between the active structure bevel and the workpiece contact surface.
features.note: This feature relates to a magnetic gripper, which is not described in the reference.

claims.quote: Flat aligner 50a may be replaced by any suitable means for positioning a wafer in a desired rotational orientation.
claims.note: The reference discloses a flat aligner for positioning a wafer in a desired rotational orientation, which is a type of positioning device for a workpiece. However, it does not specify a 'magnetic gripper' or a 'ferromagnetic workpiece'.
This reference does not disclose pole shoes, a first pole shoe, or a second pole shoe.
This reference does not disclose a magnet arranged in a housing such that, in a gripping position, a first pole shoe acts as a north pole and a second pole shoe acts as a south pole.

claims.quote: Shaft 140 is translated vertically by a conventional air-driven piston mechanism 150.
claims.note: The reference discloses a component (shaft 140) translated by an air-driven piston mechanism, which is a pneumatic means. However, it does not explicitly state that a magnet is displaceable by this mechanism, nor does it mention electrical or mechanical displacement of a magnet.
The reference describes various sensors for pressure, light, and interlocks, but does not mention a position sensor for detecting the gripping and/or release position of a magnetic gripper.
The reference describes sensors for wafer alignment and pressure, but does not mention a workpiece sensor for detecting a ferromagnetic workpiece.
The reference describes various housings and their components, but does not mention a housing with a receptacle specifically for receiving a workpiece sensor or a supply line.
The reference describes wafer handling arms and mechanisms, but does not mention a magnetic gripper or a manipulator interface for attaching a magnetic gripper to a manipulator.
This reference does not discuss magnetic grippers or housing portions designed to suppress magnetic field escape.
This reference does not discuss magnetic grippers or shielding devices to prevent magnetic field escape.
This reference does not describe a magnetic gripper system.
This reference does not describe a magnetic gripper or a ferromagnetic workpiece in the context of a magnetic gripper system.
This reference describes a wafer transport system using mechanical arms and clips, not a magnetic gripper system that presses a ferromagnetic workpiece against a contact surface using magnetic force.
This reference describes a wafer transport system using mechanical arms and clips, not a magnetic gripper system that releases a ferromagnetic workpiece by disengaging a magnetic force.
This reference does not describe a magnetic gripper system with projections having a length related to the thickness of a ferromagnetic workpiece. It describes mechanical wafer handling.
This reference describes a wafer transport system, not a magnetic gripper with a receptacle in the form of a groove.

overall.why: This reference describes a modular semiconductor wafer transport and processing system using robotic arms and vacuum chambers, which is unrelated to the subject invention of a magnetic gripper.
